profile.headline: UI/UX Advocate
profile.summary:
With over 20 years of experience in the IT industry, I've had the opportunity to work in different environments and grow based on trending technologies. From desktop to web development and back-end to front-ends, I've had exposure to a wide array of tools and development methodologies.

Excellent user interaction design abilities as well as streamlined modern graphic design for functional or marketing purposes.

Personality: Thriving Leadership, Great Enthusiasm, Out-of-the-Box Thinking

Expertise: Javascript, Typescript, Angular, UX/UI Design and Development, Graphic Design, C#, JAVA

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: In charge of software development for the Acuity team. The Acuity Micro Data Center (AMDC) is a portable data center that supports the deployment of up to 10 credir card sized servers, all within an integrated communication suite with LAN, Wi-Fi, and dual LTE network failover capabilities. It weights under 30 pounds and has a ruggedized briefcase form factor; one person can carry it around and it’s easily stowed in an airplane’s overhead compartment.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: Working hand in hand with the Technology Director to make the company and our products succeed. Among the many hats I wear: Engineering Team Scrum Master, Marketing Material Designer, UI/UX Expert, and Software Engineer.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Part of an agile driven team working for federal and government contracts. Applications are mainly web based, with high security features and government compliance standards.

positions.title: User Experience & System Integrator
positions.description: Helped prepare Electronic Health Record (EHR) and related systems to be compliant with ONC 2014 / MU Stage 2 guidelines. Acquired an in-depth knowledge of HL7 CDA Release 2 format while creating business logic modules that consumed and produced documents that adhered to the standard.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
In charge of the IT Processing Team. Among my responsibilities: development and maintenance of the Pharmacy Claims and ePrescription processing engines, maintenance of drug databases, and other business critical module.

Full exposure to the latest revisions of NCPDP and X12 standards.

positions.title: Software Architect
positions.description:
Helped implement a flexible Java/JSF development framework that eases communication between web project layers such as: JSP, Javascript and Java Beans. Lite and structured, yet compelling user interface that can be easily modified or extended with CSS.

In addition to UI/Business logic integration, I was a key player in several projects for customers in Puerto Rico and the states, helping with project architecture and resource management.

positions.title: Senior Web Developer
positions.description: In charge of the development department. Responsible for the web development life cycle standards. Designed and developed a content management system for dynamic content management on sites.

positions.title: Consultant for eSolutions / CRM divisions
positions.description: Web design and development experience using ASP web development. Multimedia material and edutainment/game development with Macromedia (now Adobe) Director. Exposure to CRM practices while developing IVR systems using Nortel Networks servers and technology.

projects.title: AEE Incidents Twitter Aggregator
projects.description: As part of the Puerto Rico Tech Summit Hackathon, we used one of the new government data APIs to retrieve all AEE reported (breakdown) incidents and publish them to a Twitter account for easier public consumption while maintaining an incident repository for possible performance analysis. Twitter account: @AEEIncidents

projects.title: SNMP Dashboard
projects.description:
On March 2, 2013 as part of my participation in the HackerLeague's HackPR UPR Mayagüez 12 hour hackathon, our team developed an SNMP alerts aggregator with a web based dashboard. Technologies used were Node.js, MongoDB, Java (for the SNMP simulator), and HTML5/CSS3 with jQuery (for the front-end).

My responsibility was to create the front-end which would frequently fetch the alerts (using ajax) and display them in the easy to manage list. As part of the features that were developed in the given 12 hours were: 3 alert lists (recent, resolved and all), persistent filtering by name, description, server and priority, and alert resolution (mark alerts as resolved.)
